lastReview.reasons: All six earlier findings are resolved. NO_PLAN is right. The decisive gap is now read from the accepted evidence: remediation benchmark $2,000-$10,000 (s2) and freelance audit benchmark $2,000-$8,000 (s3) both sit at or above the $1,500 audit-plus-remediation price, and one remediation at the low uses the whole $2,000 cap. That is ECONOMICS contradicted, with fulfilment, volume and conversion unestablished. The s1 benchmark is explicitly not treated as proof of this offer's price or of demand. The rejected DYNO Mapper $3,000-$8,000 claim is kept with its definitions reason (it includes the owner's own staff hours) and is not used. Geography is unstated on every source and a US source is required. The MARKET_VOLUME disagreement holds: about 7 buyers are needed and the lawsuit counts were rejected as a buyer count. Arithmetic checks: ($2,000 - $197) / 7 = $257; audit-only 3 x $4,000 = $12,000 with ($2,000 - $197) / 3 = $601; pre-proof $47 + $150 = $197 <= $300; captured payments by day 10 settle about day 24, and the last capture by day 16 settles by day 30. The resolution stays inside every limit and states the conditions that rule the route out.
findings: Minor: the audit-only re-scope prices at the s1 top ($4,000) and bars a provider quote at <= $600. The card's own fulfilment note says Brain writes the audit from automated scans, which could cost about $0, but that option is not considered. If Brain's audit is a credible deliverable, it changes the economics, and it needs establishing either way.
Minor: the alternatives text for the WCAG route is stale. It still says price is unestablished and does not mention the s2/s3 contradiction.

strategy.title: No executable plan: the accepted benchmarks put fulfilment cost above the $1,500 offer price
strategy.why: Three claims from two independent publishers are accepted on the accessibility card: small-site manual audits $1,500-$4,000 (s1, Accessible.org), small-business site remediation ~$2,000-$10,000 (s2, DYNO Mapper) and freelance small-site audits $2,000-$8,000 (s3, DYNO Mapper). None states its geography, so applicability to US buyers is not established. Read together they contradict the route: the offer bundles audit and remediation for $1,500, while the published low end of remediation alone ($2,000) and of a freelance audit alone ($2,000) each exceed that price, so a subcontracted delivery loses money at the benchmarks, and one remediation at the benchmark low uses the whole $2,000 total cap. A fourth claim (DYNO Mapper $3,000-$8,000 total) was rejected on definitions because it includes the owner's own staff hours. No fulfiller, buyer count, buying signal or close rate is established for any opening.

noPlan.decisiveGap: ECONOMICS is contradicted by the accepted evidence for the strongest route (cop_e0716d82a55d4527b332): published costs to deliver (remediation ~$2,000-$10,000 per site, s2; freelance audit $2,000-$8,000, s3) are at or above the $1,500 price (audit benchmark $1,500-$4,000, s1), so 7 sales would need a fulfiller at about $257 per sale, roughly one-eighth of the benchmark lows, to fit the $2,000 total cap; no such fulfiller is established, nor buyer count or close rate.
noPlan.resolution: This route stays ruled out unless a step below passes; no money is spent before step (3) proof. (1) Fulfiller, no spend, by day 2: obtain a fixed written quote from a named accessibility provider. Audit+remediation at $1,500 needs a quote <= $257 per site (7 sales, ($2,000 - $197)/7). Alternatively re-scope to audit-only priced at the s1 top ($4,000): 3 sales reach $12,000, and the quote must be <= ($2,000 - $197)/3 = about $600 per audit. Both bars sit far below the accepted benchmarks (s2 $2,000+, s3 $2,000+), so if no named provider quotes under the bar, the route is ruled out by ECONOMICS and the total-spend cap. (2) Buyer count, no spend, by day 2: a count of reachable small-business sites of the target kind from a published directory or marketplace category, plus a source stating US prices or buyers (s1-s3 state no geography). (3) Pre-proof test inside the $300 cap, line by line: Instantly Growth $47 + sending domains/mailboxes <= $150 + Brain-built lead list $0 + delivery $0 before proof = <= $197; outreach sending by day 3. Proof of demand = by day 10, at least 2 buyers have each paid the full offer price and the charge has succeeded (payment captured, not a promise or invoice); with the card's 14 days to usable cash those two settle by about day 24. (4) Timing: every remaining sale must have payment captured by day 16 so its about 14-day path to usable cash ends by day 30; if sending has not started by day 3, proof is not met by day 10, or the sales count needed cannot be captured by day 16, the 30-day window rules the route out and spending stops. Only after proof is any provider ordered, paid from receipts inside the $2,000 total.
